notable_absence.finding: No edition badge anywhere on this page, in contrast to every index page in this batch. JavaScript UDFs and the whole external-function apparatus are presented as edition-neutral. Given that Eventing-adjacent JavaScript features are commonly Enterprise-only elsewhere in the product, the absence is worth confirming with engineering rather than recorded as settled - but as documented, CREATE FUNCTION has no edition gate. Also absent: any deprecation vocabulary, consistent with the rest of the batch.

cross_product_finding: The richest access-model divergence in this batch, and it is not merely a naming difference. Server 8.0 uses a 2x2x2 RBAC ROLE matrix: {Manage, Execute} x {Global, Scope} x {inline, External} = eight named roles, of which this page names all eight across two tables. The Capella twin uses a 2x2 PRIVILEGE matrix keyed on credential type and function scope only: Basic -> Write (for both global and scoped); Advanced -> Global Function Manage (global) or Query Manage (scoped). Capella therefore has NO analogue of the inline-vs-external distinction in its access model at all, even though its prose keeps the inline/external distinction for the language feature. Consequences for reconciliation: (1) role:manage-global-external-functions and role:manage-scope-external-functions are Server-only concepts with no Capella counterpart by construction - their absence on the Capella page is not a docs gap. (2) role:manage-global-functions must NOT be merged with privilege:capella-advanced-access-global-function-manage despite the near-identical English; one is a role in Server RBAC, the other a privilege in Capella's Advanced credential model, and the promoted registry already keeps those namespaces apart. (3) Server has an Execute matrix; Capella's createfunction page has no execute-side table at all. VERSION DIVERGENCE ON THE SAME FACT: Server says 'In Couchbase Server 7.6 and later, you can create the code for an external function and the corresponding SQL++ user-defined function in a single operation.' Capella says, under a section literally headed 'Couchbase Server 7.6', 'For operational clusters using Couchbase Server 7.6 and later, you can create the code for a JavaScript function and the corresponding SQL++ user-defined function in a single operation in the Query Tab or cbq.' The Capella wording adds a cluster-type qualifier ('operational clusters') and names Capella surfaces (Query Tab, cbq) that the Server page does not - so this is a genuine adaptation, not a pure copy-paste, which slightly weakens the existing docs-issue capella-pages-cite-server-versions as an explanation for this particular instance. Finally, a DEFINITION divergence worth flagging: Server defines inline functions as 'defined using SQL++ expressions' and external functions as the JavaScript ones ('The only supported language is JavaScript'), whereas the Capella extraction record glossed n1ql:inline-function as 'Inline (SQL++ or JavaScript expression)'. The Server page does not support that gloss. Since both records now share the id n1ql:inline-function, reconciliation should adopt the Server definition and correct the Capella record's label.
version_finding: One clean availableSince: n1ql:sql-managed-user-defined-function availableSince version:server-7-6. That fact survives at 8.0 precisely because it describes a capability ADDED to a pre-existing statement, matching the pattern observed across this whole batch: version gates persist in the docs only where a new capability was bolted onto old syntax, and are absent wherever a whole statement was introduced at once. Note that 7.6 (this page) and 7.6.2 (createindex.md / createvectorindex.md defer_build) must be separate version concepts; collapsing them would lose a real distinction the docs draw. No deprecatedIn instance: nothing on this page is marked deprecated, superseded or removed, even though the 7.6 SQL++-managed form clearly supersedes the library-registration workflow for single-use functions - the docs present both as co-equal alternatives rather than marking either as the preferred or legacy path, so there is no quotable evidence for mustUseInsteadWhen or renamedFrom here either.
